text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- General Motors Corp and Canadian Auto Workers union hail strike-ending deal: Canadian automaker agrees to limits on contracting out work, gains right to sell two parts plants.
- Pact won't let General Motors turn corner on main issue: A sales drop will likely mean a 1999 fight over right to close plants.
- Corporate identity to cover library: Budget slashing prompts move.
- Ontario Premier Mike Harris unfazed by protest's opening salvo: Activists set up tent city near legislature; workers scramble to book hotel rooms.
- Prime Minister Jean Chretien bemoans woes of separatism: Montreal's economy undermined by continuing uncertainty, Chretien says.
- British telecom giant formed: Canadian companies play a key part in huge merger.
- Deal spells relief for General Motors contractors: Parts suppliers, trucking companies gearing up to recall workers, restart operations.
- Inflation holds steady: Slight rise in consumer price index, strong dollar pave way for more rate cuts.
- Auditor assails Ottawa's handling of harmonization deal: Accounting hit taken before GST signing.
- C$825 million Videotron deal: British cable unit sold to BCE subsidiary as part of huge consolidation that changes face of Britain's telecom industry.
- Canadian Auto Workers pact with General Motors cushions job-loss blow.
